Chapter Three: Life in an Orphanage and the Journey to a New Family
So, picture this: after wandering alone for what feels like forever, the boy finally catches the attention of the authorities. There’s a whirlwind of encounters—some are downright scary, others just leave him confused. Eventually, he lands in a police station, where officials do their best to unravel his story. But there’s a huge problem: the language barrier. It’s like an invisible wall that keeps him separated from anyone who might help. He tries to share where he’s from, but the words just don’t connect—his memories and place names mean nothing to the people around him.
Soon, he’s transferred to an orphanage. Imagine a place filled with kids who’ve all lost their families—a strange mix of hope and heartbreak. The orphanage is a bit of a paradox. On one hand, it’s a safe haven: there’s a bed to sleep in, regular meals, and adults who, even with their own struggles, genuinely try to care for the children. On the other hand, it’s a place of strict rules, unfamiliar routines, and a constant cloud of uncertainty. For the boy, it’s both comforting and overwhelming—a place where he’s safe, but still very much adrift.
Day after day, life in the orphanage is marked by this curious blend of hope and resignation. Some kids get lucky—they’re reunited with relatives. But for the boy, and others like him, the past is just a blur. The longing for home never really goes away, but he slowly learns to adapt. He makes a few friends, finds little moments of comfort, and even starts to imagine a future beyond those walls.
Then, one day, someone brings up the idea of adoption. It’s a moment packed with so many emotions—excitement, fear, and a sense of the unknown all at once. The thought of joining a new family, moving to a new country, and starting a brand new life? It’s almost impossible to imagine. But the alternative—staying stuck in limbo, always searching for a way back—feels just as overwhelming.
The adoption process is anything but simple. There are interviews, medical exams, and what feels like never-ending questions. And finally, he hears the news: there’s a family in Australia that wants to adopt him. Australia—it’s just a word at first, but the promise of finally belonging? That means everything. He’s given new clothes, taught a few words of English, and slowly prepared for the journey of a lifetime.
The flight to Australia is a blur—jet engines roaring, strange new foods, and the kindness of people he’s never met before. When he finally arrives, his new parents are there waiting. Right away, he feels their warmth. They welcome him not just into their house, but into their hearts—with open arms, patience, and understanding.
Adjusting to this new life isn’t easy. The language feels foreign, the customs are unfamiliar, and the landscape—well, it’s nothing like the world he left behind. But his adoptive parents are there every step of the way. They encourage him to explore, to learn, and to start building a new identity. With their support, he begins to thrive—doing well at school, making friends, and finding his place in the community. The pain of his past doesn’t disappear, but it’s softened by the love and stability he finds in his new family.
The memories of India never really fade. They become a part of him, woven together with these new experiences and fresh sources of belonging. And here’s something most people don’t realize: adoption isn’t just about swapping one family for another. It’s a complicated journey filled with questions about identity, loyalty, and loss. For the boy, it’s a transformation—an ongoing dance between who he was and who he’s becoming, between memory and reality.
As he grows, he learns how to navigate these complexities. He treasures the love of his adoptive parents, but he never stops longing for the family he lost. The search for identity becomes a big part of his life—shaping his choices and sense of self. The journey isn’t over, but for the first time in years, he feels something he hasn’t felt in a long while: real hope, and a world of possibility ahead.
